title: Illness, crutches, and learning piano
summary: Sick from the cold at the Regal Theater, he came home, was bedridden and on crutches for years, and began playing piano on a hall piano.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, very, very definitely. Him and, uh, him and Dizzy Gillespie. That's what I taught him. Yeah, both of them in the band together, see? Well, I got sick, and that's why I came back home. And, pfft, I walked on crutches for about two years and seven months. That's bad.

That's, that's bad. As a matter of fact, I stayed in bed. How long did I stay in bed? One year. One year. I stayed in bed. That's right. So, uh, then when I did get up. But where I was living at, on Village Street, they used to have old piano in the hall. And as I, I'd hippity hop from the front to the back, I used to play up by that piano, and every time I passed by, I used to bang on it. You understand? Yeah. Well, matter of fact, I couldn't play piano at that time, but I used to, I used to go play a couple of chords from me and learn how to arrange. Well, I used to play those chords, going to, and every time I'd go up and when I'd be coming back towards the room, I'd stop and bang again. So, eventually, I did that so often, until, I mean, well, since one guy went to hire me to play a job playing the piano, he couldn't find nobody else. So, I said, well, yeah, I played it. Walk out there on my crutches, and, and that's how I come to start playing piano. Well, I played piano. Matter of fact, I was, I started off, I think it was at the Dewdrop.
